channel.title: Security Brief
channel.description: Original analysis and ranked cybersecurity news with links to original sources

item.title: The edge is where attackers get in: this week's firewall, VPN and remote-access exploits
item.description: Five exploited flaws in firewalls, VPNs, remote-support software and file-sharing servers show one pattern. The systems that sit at the edge of your network, and that administrators manage remotely, are the weakest link. Here is what to check first.

item.title: October 2026 Patch Tuesday: what the Microsoft feed shows and what to do
item.description: The Microsoft feed lists few entries, and most of them are updates to October's release rather than new fixes. The one item that needs planning is a .NET remote code execution flaw that Microsoft has not fixed yet. Identity Web and WSL need version checks if you use them.

item.title: Weekly M365 & Entra Briefing: 13 to 19 October 2026
item.description: Exchange sign-in problems after October Windows Server updates, an identity-based incident at ConnectWise that affected Microsoft 365 tenants, and why device-code abuse is still worth a Conditional Access check.

item.description: Attackers are exploiting a zero-day SQL injection flaw in Arista's VeloCloud Orchestrator (VCO), the central management system for VeloCloud SD-WAN networks, the company said in an advisory on October 22. item.title: Microsoft Links Storm-0940 to ConnectWise Supply Chain Attack
item.description: The China-linked actor used an AI-enabled penetration-testing tool to automate and accelerate its attack on more than 2,200 tenants.

item.description: Cybersecurity researchers have discovered an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven intrusion ecosystem run by affiliates of the INC and The Gentlemen ransomware groups. item.title: CVE-2026-108456 Azure AI Foundry Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability
item.description: Server-side request forgery (ssrf) in Azure AI Foundry allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.

item.title: 'PHP2Shell' Bugs Signal Red Alert for Security Industry
item.description: Security teams are scrambling to remediate two critical PHP vulnerabilities following leaked details and reports of exploitation attempts.

item.title: CISA: SafePay ransomware hit over 600 critical infrastructure orgs
item.description: The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) says the SafePay ransomware gang has breached over 600 critical infrastructure organizations worldwide since 2024.

item.title: Microsoft Teams to get AI-powered, context-aware phishing detection
item.description: Microsoft has announced plans to add AI-powered phishing detection to Teams messages starting in early November 2026.

item.title: Quest Diagnostics confirms data breach exposed patient records
item.description: American clinical laboratory company Quest Diagnostics disclosed that patient records have been exposed after a threat actor gained unauthorized access to its Quanum LSM system.

item.title: CVE-2026-83862 Windows Network Load Balancing Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
item.description: Corrected the CVSS Attack Vector metric from Network (AV:N) to Adjacent (AV:A) to reflect the requirement for Layer 2 network adjacency. The CVSS base score has decreased from 9.8 to 8.8. This is an informational change only. Customers who have successfully installed the update do not need to take any further action.

item.title: Hacker leaks 281 GB of data from Germany’s far-right AfD party
item.description: The AfD has confirmed that hackers breached its hosting provider. A leak site now claims to offer 421,179 of the party’s internal emails, and shows AI-written summaries rather than the emails themselves. Read more in my article on the Hot for Security blog.

item.title: AI Agents as Insider Threats: Inside Microsoft's Bet on a Unified Security Stack
item.description: Microsoft's Project Perception adds Guardian Agents to monitor and contain anomalous AI agents, but experts warn that policing unpredictable agents with other agents may compound — not contain — the risk.

item.title: Critical x402 SDK Flaw Could Let Malicious APIs Drain AI Agents’ Token Balances
item.description: AI agents paying for API calls with the x402 SDKs could sign a payment for their full balance of a supported token if a malicious API asked for it, security firm V12 said on October 22. The cause was the SDKs' default client, which set no spending limit until releases on August 18 added one. The risk was limited to…

item.title: 11 Million Impacted by Capcom Data Breach
item.description: The hackers stole 11 million email addresses from CAPCOM ID and changed the login passwords for 196 accounts. The post 11 Million Impacted by Capcom Data Breach appeared first on SecurityWeek.

item.title: Reports of PHP bug exploitation attempts grow as experts downplay viability of exploits
item.description: The headline-grabbing bugs known colloquially as PHP2Shell are giving cyber analysts a lot to track — and a lot to debunk.

item.title: Machine speed attacks require machine speed detection and response
item.description: Attackers can steal credentials and begin exfiltrating data within minutes, often before security teams can respond. Exaforce examines real-world attacks involving stolen GitHub tokens, malicious AI installers, and MFA phishing, explaining why faster detection and automated containment are critical.

item.title: Critical Flaw in Python’s Popular Pillow Image Library Allows Code Execution via a Crafted Image
item.description: Pillow, the most widely used image library for Python, can be made to run operating system commands on a server by specifying the name of a file it is told to open. The flaw, CVE-2026-112900, is in the way Pillow handles EPS images, which it opens by passing the file's name to Ghostscript, a separate program it runs…
